# Vertical overlay: Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services

**Level:** NAICS 2022 sector 54 (parent vertical)
**Primary industry for Cris Santos Company:** NAICS 541211 Offices of Certified Public Accountants. CPA and tax preparation firm.
**Primary system:** Tax preparation software and client document portal

## Regulators and sector risk management agency
Federal Trade Commission (FTC) Enforces the GLBA Safeguards Rule for tax preparers/accountants and FTC Act Section 5 data security; Internal Revenue Service (IRS) Tax-preparer data protection (IRC 7216; Pub 4557 guidance; e-file provider rules); DoD (CMMC Program) / FAR Council / GSA Federal contractor safeguarding (FAR 52.204-21, DFARS 252.204-7012, CMMC); HHS Office for Civil Rights HIPAA enforcement for firms acting as business associates; State bars / state boards of accountancy Professional conduct and confidentiality rules (state-adopted; not federal)

## Primary regulation for the gap analysis (P03)
**FTC Safeguards Rule**, 16 CFR Part 314. It is the only broad, binding written-security-program rule that reaches the largest group of small professional firms (every tax-preparing CPA or accounting practice). Its nine prescriptive elements (314.4(a)-(i)) make clear, auditable gap criteria with a built-in small-firm carve-out (314.6). For DoD contractors, use NIST SP 800-171 / CMMC Level 2 instead. For law firms, pair it with state-adopted ABA Rule 1.6(c).
Source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/part-314

## Sector context
- **Sensitive data:** Federal Tax Information / tax return information (IRC 7216); SSNs, bank and account numbers (GLBA customer information); Attorney-client privileged and confidential client information; PHI held as a HIPAA business associate; Federal Contract Information (FCI) and Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI); Client IP and trade secrets, M&A material non-public information
- **Critical systems:** Tax preparation and e-file software; Document/practice management systems (DMS, e-discovery); Client portals and secure file transfer; Email and M365/Google Workspace tenants; Accounting/ERP and time & billing; RMM/PSA tools (MSPs and IT consultants); GCC-High / CUI enclaves for defense contractors
- **Sector AI rules and guidance:** Colorado SB26-189 (Automated Decision-Making Technology) Colo. SB26-189 (repeals and reenacts SB24-205) Duties for developers and deployers of ADMT used in consequential decisions on employment, education, financial/lending, housing, insurance, health care and government services. Relevant to consulting firms that build or deploy such tools.; ABA Formal Opinion 512 (Generative AI tools) ABA Standing Committee on Ethics and Professional Responsibility, Formal Op. 512 (July 2024) Ethics guidance applying competence, confidentiality, communication and fee rules to lawyers' use of generative AI. Not law.
- **Assurance alternatives to SOC 2:** SOC 1 and SOC 2 reports are core services of CPA firms; client assurance via engagement letters
- **Scenario incident (P08):** Business email compromise and taxpayer data theft
- **Scenario AI use case (P10):** Generative AI for tax and document preparation

## Notes
NAICS 54 has no single sector regulator; obligations depend on client data. Status checks: FAR CUI rule (FR Doc 2024-30437) and FAR incident reporting rule (FR Doc 2023-21328) are still proposed. A FAR Overhaul proposed rule (FR Doc 2026-12559) was published June 23, 2026. All 50 states, DC and the territories have breach notification statutes with differing triggers, deadlines and regulator-notice duties. They are not enumerated here.
